about.what_body: A volunteer-run aggregation site for the 26 August 2026 Bhote Koshi / Trishuli flood. We pull every public data source into one place every {cadence}, show official numbers side by side with their sources, and let anyone add what they know in under five minutes. Per place, we show how many people are believed there, how many are confirmed reached, and how many are unknown.
about.not_body: Not an official source, and it must never be treated as one. Not a missing-persons registry — the Nepal Police and Red Cross run those, and we point you to them at the top of every page. We publish observed status only: no hazard predictions, no danger ratings for villages.
about.why_body: Each agency counts something different: NDRRMA counts everyone reported out of contact; the Police count confirmed missing-person reports; MoFA counts foreigners reported to embassies; the Tourism Department counts tourists on agency manifests; the PM’s portal counts every report submitted, including duplicates. We show them all rather than choosing one.
about.handling_1: Names, contacts and photos are stripped and encrypted on arrival; the public site shows counts, places, statuses and times only.
about.handling_2: Full reports go to Nepal Police and MoFA through an agreed channel, with your permission flag attached (on by default).
about.handling_3: Every public number carries its source and an “as of” time. We never blend sources into a single invented figure.
about.handling_4: Everything is deletable: from “My folder” you can withdraw a contribution and it leaves the public counts within {cadence}.
about.who_body: A volunteer team of Nepali and international engineers, data people and translators, working with Nepali partners. No agency affiliation, no funding to disclose, no ads, no tracking beyond an anonymous visit counter.
about.agencies_body: Want a data feed, a correction channel, or to endorse? Everything we hold is exportable as CSV/JSON with source attribution per cell. Write to us — we answer within hours.

corridor.illustrative: Illustrative, not a hydraulic model. The clock follows the recorded front (DHM river watch, USGS, ICIMOD); the lake volume starts at the figure China's MWR published. Nothing here is a forecast.
corridor.phase_collapse: 08:37 — a ~600 m section of glacier and rock falls into the Lhende Khola (USGS records it as M5.2)
corridor.phase_breach: The barrier lake breaches. Gyirong Port is hit seven minutes later — about 190 km/h over the first 22 km
corridor.phase_wave: The wave runs the corridor: Timure 08:45 · Syabrubesi 08:50 · Betrawati 09:20 · Galchhi 10:28 · Devghat 13:00
